prompt: A hypothetical open-pit gold project reports, at a 0.4 g/t Au cut-off, an Indicated Mineral Resource of 12.4 Mt at 1.35 g/t Au and an Inferred Mineral Resource of 5.1 Mt at 1.10 g/t Au. Metallurgical testwork on composite samples supports 91% gold recovery. The company's presentation states the project 'hosts 0.65 Moz of recoverable gold'. (a) Calculate the contained gold in each category in thousand troy ounces. (b) Calculate the recoverable gold in the Indicated category. (c) Comment on whether the 0.65 Moz recoverable statement is correct and appropriate under the JORC Code or NI 43-101.
reference_answer: (a) Indicated: 12.4 Mt x 1.35 g/t = 16.74 t Au = 16,740,000 g / 31.1035 g per troy oz = 538.2 koz. Inferred: 5.1 Mt x 1.10 g/t = 5.61 t Au = 180.4 koz. Total contained 718.6 koz. (b) Indicated recoverable = 538.2 x 0.91 = 489.8 koz. (c) Total recoverable across both categories would be 718.6 x 0.91 = 653.9 koz, so the 0.65 Moz figure is arithmetically the sum of Indicated and Inferred recoverable ounces. It is not appropriate: Mineral Resources are reported as in-situ contained metal, not recoverable metal, and Inferred material has too low a level of geological confidence to be combined with Indicated as if it were equivalent; reporting standards discourage aggregating Inferred with higher categories without clear disclosure. Recoverable metal belongs with a mine plan and a Reserve or an economic study that discloses the Inferred proportion.

rubric.criterion: Uses troy ounces (31.1035 g) to convert grams of gold to ounces, not avoirdupois ounces.
Identifies that the 0.65 Moz figure equals Indicated plus Inferred recoverable ounces combined.
States that Inferred resources should not be aggregated with Indicated as if equivalent, because of their lower geological confidence.
Notes that Mineral Resources are reported as in-situ (contained) metal, and that quoting recoverable ounces from resources is a misleading convention.

sources.citation: JORC Code 2012 edition (Joint Ore Reserves Committee), sections on Inferred Mineral Resources and reporting of Mineral Resources
CIM Definition Standards for Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves (2014)

review_notes: Trap: the promotional figure is arithmetically right but sums Inferred with Indicated and quotes recoverable metal from a resource. Reviewer to confirm preferred wording on aggregation (JORC Clause references not checked against the PDF).
